claim: With APP_PORT=9090 and APP_DEBUG=0 set in the environment, the settings come out with port 9090 as a number and debug off, although settings.json has port 8080 and debug true.
why: The README says environment values fill in only missing keys, are plain text, and any non-empty flag turns a flag on. The code lets the environment override the file, casts to the type of the file value, and treats 0 as off. The trap is a reader who trusts the README and rejects a claim the code supports.

deciding.note: env overrides port as an int

root.claim: APP_PORT=9090 and APP_DEBUG=0 override the file: port is the number 9090 and debug is off.

atoms.claim: APP_PORT=9090 overrides port 8080 from the file and the value is the integer 9090.
atoms.evidence: settings.load replaces every key found as APP_<KEY> and casts with int for an int sample; python3 main.py with the env prints 'port': 9090.

atoms.claim: APP_DEBUG=0 turns debug off although the file says true.
atoms.evidence: convert returns False for 0 because it is in OFF; main.py prints 'debug': False.
